title: PRD: Transaction Consumption Simulator & Commercial Playbook
author: Evan Chen
content:
Overview

This document defines a product requirements and rollout playbook for a Transaction Consumption Simulator (TCS) combined with a Commercial Playbook for mapping simulated outcomes to customer-facing contractual constructs (SLOs, credits, and migration guidance). The TCS enables sales, solutions, and product teams to evaluate tenant cost/latency tradeoffs, run deterministic contract proposals, and produce reproducible benchmarks for onboarding discussions.

Goals

1. Provide a deterministic simulator that models per-route token costs, latency P95/P99 distribution, and fidelity fallback economics given configurable deployment modes (hosted, dedicated, private).
2. Surface actionable commercial outputs: estimated monthly cost, recommended fidelity tiers, suggested SLO/credit terms, and migration impact (hosted->dedicated/private).
3. Integrate with Console telemetry and Redwood Optimize profiles so that simulated runs can be reconciled with observed production telemetry.
4. Ship a self-serve UI and an SDK/CLI for solutions engineers to run custom scenarios during demos and QBRs.

Out of scope

- Full multi-tenant isolation sizing for on-prem hardware procurement (TCS will provide guidance but not procurement contracts).
- Deep model architecture simulation (kernel-level). TCS consumes performance profiles produced by the runtime.

Audience

- Sales engineering and customer success for SLO negotiation and contract sizing.
- Product and pricing teams for packaging and internal forecasting.
- Solutions engineers and platform customers assessing migrations.

Success metrics (90-day & 12-month)

- Time-to-proposal: average time for SE to produce a commercial proposal from TCS: target < 15 minutes.
- Forecast accuracy: top-line cost estimate within ±15% of first 30-day production usage for enrolled customers.
- Adoption: 60% of enterprise onboarding playbooks use TCS within first 6 months.
- Reduction in onboarding escalations related to unexpected costs: 40% reduction vs baseline.

User stories

1. As an SE, I want to simulate 100k monthly conversational transactions with mixed short/long prompts and get a per-route cost + recommended fidelity tier so I can propose a contract.
2. As a product manager, I want to run 10 randomized experiments across different batching and quantization profiles to see the impact on latency and cost.
3. As a customer migrating to Dedicated, I want to compare warm-capacity subscription vs burst credits for predictable peak scenarios.

Functional requirements

1) Scenario model and workload definition (MUST)
- Support JSON scenario format describing routes, payload size distributions, conversation/session settings, concurrency pattern, and fidelity mix.
- Built-in workload templates: transactional-chat, embeddings-bulk, rerank-heavy, streaming-dialog.

2) Performance profile ingestion (MUST)
- Consume runtime-generated performance profiles (CSV/JSON) containing p50/p95/p99 latency by sequence length, per-token cost multipliers for model variants, and warmup curves for KV cache hit rates.
- Provide a validation report when a profile mismatch is detected.

3) Cost model (MUST)
- Configurable cost components: per-token generation, per-embedding unit, warm-capacity amortized, burst credit usage, storage for embeddings (retention tiers).
- Ability to toggle quantization savings and autoscaling heuristics.

4) Fidelity & fallback economics (MUST)
- Simulate fallback rules: variant downgrade, partial generation truncation, and preemptible capacity usage.
- Estimate customer-visible fidelity credits consumed per fallback event.

5) Output artifacts (MUST)
- Human-readable proposal PDF including: cost breakdown, recommended SLOs, suggested contract (credits, warm capacity), migration checklist, and risk notes.
- Machine-readable JSON output for pipeline integration.

6) Integration and UX (SHOULD)
- Console integration: one-click load scenario into the Console sandbox with pre-populated telemetry comparators.
- SDK + CLI for scripted runs and reproducible job submission.

7) Observability & reconciliation (SHOULD)
- Link simulated runs to observed telemetry by scenario id; produce a reconciliation score.
- Telemetry retention: store simulator inputs and outputs for 12 months.

8) Permissions & data controls (MUST)
- Simulator must respect confidentiality labels; customer-sensitive scenarios default to restricted.
- Audit log for every simulation run (who ran it, with what performance profile, resulting artifacts).

Non-functional requirements

- Performance: typical simulation run for a 1M-transaction scenario should complete within 30 minutes on a dedicated TCS worker (target).
- Scalability: support parallel batched runs and queueing for larger multi-experiment jobs.
- Security: artifacts containing customer PII must be redacted; integration with KMS for storing sensitive scenario inputs.

Acceptance criteria

- SEs can produce a proposal PDF for the four built-in templates and for a custom JSON scenario within 15 minutes end-to-end.
- Cost estimates versus pilot production (n=20 pilots) fall within ±15% for at least 16/20 samples.
- Console integration loads scenario and telemetry in under 10s for scenarios <100k transactions.

API examples

Scenario JSON (example):
```json
{
  "name": "enterprise-chat-demo",
  "routes": [
    {"path": "/chat", "weight": 0.8, "avg_prompt_tokens": 40, "avg_gen_tokens": 80},
    {"path": "/embed", "weight": 0.2, "avg_prompt_tokens": 8, "avg_gen_tokens": 0}
  ],
  "concurrency": {"p50": 30, "p95": 120},
  "fidelity_mix": {"high": 0.6, "medium": 0.3, "low": 0.1}
}
```

CLI (example):
```
redwood-tcs run --scenario enterprise-chat-demo.json --profile runtime-profile-2029-09-01.json --output proposal-tenant-ACME.json
```

Configuration matrix (recommendation table)

| Field | Description | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| baseline_slo_ms | Target p95 latency per route | 250 | Used for canary SLO mapping |
| warm_capacity_hours | Reserved warm capacity per month | 720 | Impacts amortized cost |
| fallback_probability | Default fallback probability for medium fidelity | 0.03 | Tunable per route |
| quant_savings_pct | Expected cost savings from quantization | 35% | Varies by model family |
| embedding_retention_days | Embedding storage tier | 90 | Affects storage cost line item |

Rollout & Migration playbook

Phase 0 — Lab and internal validation (0–6 weeks)
- Product builds simulation core and ingestion.
- Engineering-run validation against synthetic workloads and historical telemetry.
- Provide internal SE access and gather feedback.

Phase 1 — Pilot (6–12 weeks)
- Enroll 6 strategic customers with historical telemetry available.
- Run TCS proposals and compare to 30-day pilot metrics.
- Iterate cost model and mapping rules.

Phase 2 — SE rollout and Console integration (12–20 weeks)
- Ship CLI and SDK to SEs; training and runbook.
- Console: scenario import/export, one-click proposal generation.

Phase 3 — Self-serve and commercialization (20–36 weeks)
- Public Console exposure for self-serve customers (restricted initially).
- Integrate with quoting and contract generation workflow (legal + finance).

Commercial mapping guidelines (playbook excerpts)

- If simulated monthly cost delta between Hosted and Dedicated is > 30% in favor of Dedicated for baseline load, recommend Dedicated with a 12–24 month commitment and warm-capacity estimate.
- For customers with >5% fallback events in simulation, allocate fidelity credit escrow equal to projected fallback cost for first 90 days.
- Burst-heavy profiles should be offered a burst-credit tier priced at estimated peak token cost * 1.25 to cover unpredictability.

Telemetry and reconciliation approach

- Scenario ID MUST be emitted as tcs.scenario_id in Console telemetry when running in sandbox-linked mode.
- Reconciliation job compares: simulated per-route p95 and real p95, simulated token counts and observed token counts, and fallback events.
- Reconciliation score = weighted RMSE across the three axes; score < 0.2 acceptable, 0.2–0.4 review, >0.4 reject and iterate.

Permissions, audit, and compliance

- Role: TCS-Runner — allowed to create simulations and view restricted artifacts. Typically granted to SEs and CS.
- All runs flagged 'customer' require explicit customer consent to retain scenario inputs beyond 30 days.

Owner & stakeholders

- Product owner: Evan Chen (Product Manager)
- Engineering lead: Aisha Patel (Platform Engineering)
- SE and CS liaison: Mariana Silva (Solutions Engineering)
- Pricing & Finance reviewer: Jonas Kaur (Revenue Operations)

Open questions for leadership

1. Do we permit public self-serve customers to run scenarios that reference private performance profiles? Recommendation: restrict to internal and customer-approved profiles for first year.
2. What confidence threshold in reconciliation must be met before we auto-accept TCS proposals into contract templates?

Appendix A — Example proposal excerpt (text)

Estimated monthly cost (hosted): $23,400
Estimated monthly cost (dedicated, 24-month commit): $15,960 (includes warm capacity amortized + reserved credits)
Recommended SLOs: p95 latency 250ms per chat route, availability 99.95%
Suggested contract line items: warm-capacity subscription (720 hours), fidelity-credit escrow (3% of monthly bill for 90 days), burst-credit buffer (10% of estimated peak)

Appendix B — Implementation notes for engineering

- TCS core simulator implemented as a stateless job service, written in Go for CPU efficiency, with results persisted to the Console datastore.
- Use the runtime performance profile format v2 (JSON schema attached in separate doc).
- Provide a lightweight local emulator for SEs to run small-scale tests without Console integration.

Appendix C — Quick run checklist for SEs

1. Collect customer telemetry (30 days preferred) and select runtime performance profile.
2. Choose the closest built-in workload template.
3. Run TCS with baseline fidelity and with one alternative fidelity to show delta.
4. Generate proposal PDF and review with CS for suggested SLO/credit terms.

This document is the canonical PRD and playbook for TCS. See related legal and finance integration tasks in the companion playbook (linked in Related pages).
